# Experimental read-only native successor publication

This test-mod-only increment builds forward from report 87b2d81d714f5660c3e6bdac93db2fab2a785f00 and reuses the unchanged fence evidence at 87c2b6383ea528b1d604f415c0ffab49131884ac (run 44019522739). It does not add production source sets, mixins, admission settings, an unrestricted unlock or a playable-party release.

## Bounded policy

A completed, exactly verified staged return may retire its deny-all access policy into a durable READ_ONLY successor epoch. Original identity reservations and revocation tombstones remain intact. The successor grants only explicitly selected native reads and unchanged-state save acknowledgements through one bound synthetic manager/factory. Gameplay mutations and send-out remain denied. This is a pre-playable publication component, not end-to-end custody.

A separate GenerationJournal binds the source/custody generation, owner, provider, source hash, monotonic epoch and phase. PREPARED precedes fresh construction and cache insertion; READ_ONLY commits before access is granted. Missing, mismatched or PREPARED state refuses recovery. A clean committed or suspended epoch requires full source/destination and cache revalidation plus fresh reconstruction before another epoch can become accessible. A failed publication never falls back to native backups.

Freshness is based on constructor-return hooks during a non-inheritable private reconstruction capability, not UUID equality. Only the constructor-tracked detached graph can be initialized in that capability. Exact full native state is checked before publication and permitted access. A previous object, forged same-UUID clone, previous-epoch reference, stale iterator or unrelated provider receives no successor permission.

The legacy native fence itself is unchanged. The new policy is compiled only in the disposable test mod; original generated wrappers are redirected in the private harness. Reconstruction is limited to the reviewed synthetic class/topology/profile and exact frozen source. It is not approval of arbitrary callbacks, custom data or third-party code.

## Mixed-owner lifecycle

For the explicitly bound scratch factory, native saveAll partitions dirty stores. Quarantined or revoked stores remain dirty with a recorded denial; unrelated stores retain native saving. Read-only successor saves verify unchanged complete state and existing durable/native records, then clear only that fresh store's dirty entry. They do not fabricate a receipt for Cobblemon's asynchronous saver.

Previously queued native single/batch saves reject fenced payloads per entry without aborting unrelated entries in the same batch. A rejected write never becomes a successful save receipt. Unexpected IO failures are not swallowed by that handling.

The real native autosave subscription remains enabled. Native shutdown is joined outside the native method lock. Disconnect suspends the epoch and revokes its objects; explicit republishing requires a new generation and fresh graph. A narrow request adapter returns an explicit unavailable result without creating an empty fallback party. Actual gameplay packet handlers are not yet wired to that adapter.

## Still excluded

No nonempty-party jail admission, gameplay release, battle/riding/trade capability, ordinary post-release mutable save contract or actual player handback is enabled. The tests operate on synthetic scratch owners and independent native manager/factory instances, not the normal global player's conversion-backed provider. Full modpack and occupied-save migration still need exact private copies. No installed files, real worlds/player data, certificates, companion requirements, wallet behavior or model settings are modified.

The trusted local filesystem and journal assumptions remain those of the prior generation implementation. Process halts are not physical power-loss certification or protection against privileged whole-directory rollback, reflection or arbitrary direct filesystem writes.
